attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 23 Ιουνίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder's Romanian row already carries, and she is the only Agrippina in the corpus. The details settle it: born and martyred at Rome, she refused marriage for the love of her heavenly bridegroom, and after her death three Christian women, Bassa, Paula and Agathonike, took her body and after much wandering came to Sicily and buried it there. The page's heading reads «(; - 262)» and its narrative puts her denunciation in «Το 262 μ.Χ.»; no `dates` object is proposed, because the year comes from this second source alone and the folder's own source gives none. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence.

attestations.note: The day’s first entry, and the only one of the four that is one person. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of this wave is. The Julian 23 June is the same menologion number this folder’s other venerated rows carry, so there is no second day and no §4 note is owed. **A YEAR IS WRITTEN WHERE THE FOLDER HAD NONE, WHICH IS NOT A WIDENING AND NOT A NARROWING.** `dates` was null before today. This book ends the entry „Упокојила се и славом увенчала 275. године.“ — she reposed and was crowned with glory in the year 275. `death` earliest 275, latest 275, display «275», basis traditional, the sentence in the note. doxologia gives no year, and this folder’s own prose already says so in those words. **AND THE BOOK DOES NOT SIT WITH ITSELF, AND NOTHING IS REPAIRED.** The same entry has „пострада у време цара Валеријана.“, she suffered in the time of the emperor Valerian, whose reign ran out fifteen years before the year the entry ends with. **An emperor is no source for a year and a reign is not a date**, so nothing is derived from Valerian, nothing is averaged and nothing is adjusted: both statements are this book’s own and both are written as they stand. A reader does not repair a source. This is the same shape the Julian 22 June found in the entry that dated a council to 361 and put it in the reign of Jovian; two days running, so it is a habit of the book and not an accident.  **saint.gr’S 262 IS NOT WRITTEN FROM HERE, AND THE WIDENING IS THE AUTHOR’S.** This folder’s prose carries the Greek page’s «in the year 262 she was denounced to the authorities» — a year the folder has cited and never recorded, which is exactly what `date-citation-audit.mjs` exists to print. It stays unwritten for two separate reasons. The Prologue is this day’s source and 262 is out of a book this reading did not open, which is the ruling the Julian 22 June made over saint.gr’s 303. And the Greek sentence hangs its year on the **denunciation**, where this book’s 275 is of the repose outright — and a year of a denunciation is no more a death than a year of a burial or of a relic-finding is. Whether the field should widen to «262 or 275» is the author’s to decide and is named for it. **AND THE AUDIT MOVES, MEASURED BOTH WAYS.** Before: `date-audit` undated 1619, no-birth 2779, stated 153, and **this folder was in none of the three**—`--list stated` returns no row for it, because the «262» sentence in its prose carries no verb in that audit’s death list. After: undated 1618 and no-birth 2780, each by one and both by this folder; `stated` stays 153, and the folder is now out of that check altogether, having a `death`. **`types` UNTOUCHED.** The heading gives Света, which is not a rank, and мученица, which is the `martyr` the folder carries; the body corroborates the `virgin` beside it with „налевајући срце своје благоухањем девичке чистоте, девствености и целомудрености.“ and with „Обручена беше Христу Господу, и као невеста Христова пострада у време цара Валеријана.“, but a type already held is not written twice and a rank read out of a body is not written at all. No `office`. No `locations`: Rome and the island of Sicily are named in clauses. **NO ROWS, AND RULING 3 REFUSES THREE WOMEN.** „Њене другарице: Васа, Пауна и Агатоника пренеше мошти њене на острво Сицилију, и тамо их чесно сахранише.“ — her companions Vasa, Pauna and Agathonica carried her relics to the island of Sicily and buried them honourably. `ls saints | grep -iE '^(bassa|vassa|vasa|paula|pauna|agathonic)'` returns `bassa-of-edessa`, `bassa-of-jerusalem`, `bassa-of-tyre`, `paula-companion-of-lucillian` and `agathonica-sister-of-papylas`, and not one of them is a companion of this woman: an identification off a bare forename is not an identification. No folder, no row — and the three names are already in this folder’s prose off the other two books, so nothing is added there either. **The second name differs between the books and is recorded and not resolved**: this one has «Пауна», Pauna, where the folder’s Romanian account has Paula and its Greek one Paule. No `sr` form is written off a woman who has no folder. **THE DEDICATION AND THE WONDER TAKE NO ROWS EITHER.** „Ту се доцније подиже црква у име свете Агрипине.“ — a church was raised there afterwards in her name, and a dedication is not a relation. „Силом њених моштију чак и Агарјани беху враћени од града, где те мошти почиваху.“ — by the power of her relics even the Agarenes were turned back from the town where they lay, which is the same deliverance the Romanian account in this folder gives, so two books agree on it; the object of a wonder is not its subject and the Agarenes are nobody’s folder. The emperor Valerian takes no row. **A MISPRINT IN THE BOOK, RECORDED AND NOT REPAIRED.** „Он њених моштију биваху чудеса безбројна.“ stands where the sense wants Од, from her relics; Он is he. It is the page’s own letter, a reader does not mend a source, and the clause is not quoted in the life. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse. THE VERSE IS NOT USED. The ПЕСМА for 23 June is twenty-two lines on the first entry alone and nothing at all on the second, third or fourth: it calls Agrippina purer than the lily, has her chant psalms in her wounds and bless her persecutors, has the angel come down when her bones are broken, and ends by asking her prayers. It is Bishop Nikolai’s own verse and not the entry’s account, so §3 of this wave’s brief puts it in no field and in no life, and it is recorded here instead. **That it versifies one of four entries is worth the line**: the verse is no index of what a day holds. **WHAT THIS DAY REFUSES, AND IT REFUSES A WHOLE ENTRY TWICE OVER.** The Prologue prints four entries for the Julian 23 June and only two of them are people. The third, „Спомен иконе Пресвете Богородице Владимирске“, is the commemoration of the Vladimir icon of the Mother of God and a feast and not a folder, by the standing ruling; its body is about a battle, not a life, and the two men in it — the Tatar khan Ahmet and the prince Ivan Vasilyevich who went out with the army — are neither of them saints of the entry and neither takes a row. The fourth, „Повест о покајању Теофила“, is **the shape this wave has not met before**: a heading that is not a commemoration at all but a tale, «a story of the repentance of Theophilus», about a man who out of envy signed away his soul, repented, wept forgiveness out of the Most Pure after a forty-day fast, got his paper back and confessed in church, and whose face shone like the sun when the bishop absolved him; it ends by saying God does not only forgive true penitents but numbers them among the saints. **No folder, on two grounds at once.** It is not a saint’s heading: there is no rank word in it, the noun it leads with is a tale and the person is in the genitive after it. And **Ruling 3**: `ls saints | grep -i theophil` returns twenty-three Theophilus folders and not one of them is this man — no penitent, nobody on 23 June, nobody of Adana, and `grep -l enitent saints/*/saint.json` returns five folders of which none is a Theophilus. He is named here and left out of the prose, and no row and no folder is made for him.

hymns.text: Mieluşeaua Ta, Iisuse, Agripina, strigă cu glas mare: pe Tine, Mirele meu, te iubesc și pe Tine căutându-Te mă chinuiesc și împreună mă răstignesc și împreună mă îngrop cu Botezul Tău; și pătimesc pentru Tine, ca să împărățesc întru Tine; și mor pentru tine, ca să viez pentru Tine; ci, ca o jertfă fără de prihană, primește-mă pe mine ceea ce cu dragoste mă jertfesc Ție. Pentru rugăciunile ei, ca un milostiv, mântuiește sufletele noastre.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfintei Mucenițe Agripina, glasul 4; the text is the common of a woman martyr, printed with her name in it.

english.text: Thy lamb Agrippina, O Jesus, cries out with a loud voice: Thee, my Bridegroom, do I love, and seeking Thee I am in torment; with Thee I am crucified and with Thee I am buried in Thy baptism; I suffer for Thee that I may reign in Thee, and I die for Thee that I may live for Thee. Accept me, then, as a spotless offering, who sacrifice myself to Thee in love. At her prayers, O merciful One, save our souls.

hymns.text: Θεῖον Πνεύματι, κραταιωθεῖσα, ἠνδραγάθησας, γενναιοφρόνως, Ἀγριππίνα παρθενίας ὀσφράδιον ὅθεν Χριστοῦ δοξασθεῖσα τὴ χάριτι, πηγᾶς θαυμάτων βλυστάνεις τοὶς πέρασι. Μάρτυς ἔνδοξε, Χριστὸν τὸν Θεὸν ἱκέτευε, δωρήσασθαι ἠμὶν τὸ μέγα ἔλεος.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος γ’, Θείας πίστεως — the only apolytikion on the page of «Αγία Αγριππίνα», and it names her

english.text: Made strong by the divine Spirit, you played the man with a noble mind, Agrippina, sweet savour of virginity; and so, glorified by the grace of Christ, you pour out springs of wonders to the ends of the earth. Glorious martyr, entreat Christ our God that great mercy may be given us.

hymns.text: Агница Твоя, Иисусе, Агрипина/ зовет велиим гласом:/ Тебе, Женише мой, люблю,/ и, Тебе ищущи, страдальчествую,/ и сраспинаюся, и спогребаюся крещению Твоему,/ и стражду Тебе ради,/ яко да царствую в Тебе,/ и умираю за Тя, да и живу с Тобою;/ но яко жертву непорочную приими мя,/ с любовию пожершуюся Тебе.// Тоя молитвами, яко Милостив, спаси души наша.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 23 июня ст. ст. — «Тропарь мученицы Агриппины», глас 4. The common troparion of a virgin-martyr — «Агница Твоя, Иисусе» — with her name set in it, printed under her name.

english.text: Thy lamb, O Jesus, Agrippina, cries out with a loud voice: Thee, my Bridegroom, I love, and seeking Thee I contend, and am crucified and buried with Thee in Thy baptism; I suffer for Thy sake, that I may reign in Thee, and I die for Thee, that I may live with Thee. Receive me as a spotless sacrifice, offered to Thee with love. At her prayers, as Thou art merciful, save our souls.

hymns.text: Светлых подвиг твоих светоносный наста день,/ воньже почитающи сих, Божественная Церковь/ вся созывает весело вопити тебе:/ радуйся, дево и мученице,// Агрипино всечестная.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 23 июня ст. ст. — «Кондак мученицы Агриппины», глас 4. Proper to her: «Агрипино всечестная» in the vocative, and the page spells the name with one п here as the folder already did.

english.text: The light-bearing day of thy radiant struggles is come, on which the divine Church, honouring them, calls all together to cry out to thee with gladness: rejoice, virgin and martyr, all-honoured Agrippina.

death.note: The folder held no date of any kind until today. The Охридски пролог for 23. јун ст. ст. ends the entry „Упокојила се и славом увенчала 275. године.“ — she reposed and was crowned with glory in the year 275. doxologia gives no year, as this folder’s own prose says. saint.gr’s «262», which that prose also carries, is the year of her **denunciation** and not of her death, and is out of a book this reading did not open; it is not written here and the question of widening to «262 or 275» is named for the author. The same entry puts her suffering in the reign of the emperor Valerian, which ended before 275; an emperor is no source for a year, nothing is derived from it and nothing is repaired (5 October 2026).
